final_message:
I finished the privileged gap-analysis memo for the General Counsel, about 12,500 words; it passed the docx validator and parse-doc reads it back. It covers 16 gaps and finds the Side A coverage strong, with the critical gaps at the change-of-control tail, the insured-vs-insured exclusion and the biotech-specific exclusions. The policy and broker summary also name the company and the insurer inconsistently.

failed.title: ISSUE_006: Analyzes asymmetry scenarios between the two standards
failed.reasoning: Memo does not analyze divergent outcomes, such as denial of indemnification under the good-faith determination while D&O coverage continues, or the reverse; Gap 11 only addresses venue and lead-in.

failed.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies contribution cap under indemnification agreement
failed.reasoning: Gap 15 identifies the §10 12-month compensation cap but does not discuss how it interacts with D&O policy limits.

failed.title: ISSUE_008: Analyzes exposure when insurance limits are exhausted
failed.reasoning: Gap 7 notes that indemnification becomes an uninsured Company cost after exhaustion, but it does not analyze a claim exceeding the $50M capacity in terms of the contribution provision, the Indemnitee cap and unlimited Company exposure.

failed.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies subrogation conflict between policy and agreement
failed.reasoning: Memo treats subrogation as 'Aligned' and does not identify a potential circular subrogation conflict between Policy §12.2 and Agreement §13.

failed.title: ISSUE_009: Explains circular subrogation practical implications
failed.reasoning: No analysis of the practical implications of circular subrogation is provided.

failed.title: ISSUE_010: References ERISA § 410(a) or explains why ERISA claims create unique D&O coverage gaps
failed.reasoning: No reference to ERISA §410(a) or to ERISA limits on indemnification; the memo only notes this Policy's exclusion and recommends a fiduciary policy, without explaining why ERISA claims are a distinctive gap.
